TURNING DOWNTOWN KL INTO AN AR PLAYGROUND

42 artists, 35 artworks, one QR code apiece — how ARFestKL became a city-wide AR trail with no app to download.

Client
ARFestKL
Technology
WebAR · 8th Wall
Location
Downtown KL
Read time
6 min

ARFestKL wanted to turn the city centre itself into a gallery — no walls to rent, no building to book, just Kuala Lumpur's own streets carrying 42 artists' work for a weekend.

The brief was ambitious in a specific way: 35 AR artworks spread across more than 30 physical touchpoints between Bukit Bintang, Pasar Seni and Dataran Merdeka, and every single one of them had to be frictionless for a stranger walking past. No app store, no account, no tutorial — point a phone, and the art appears.

The scale problem

Getting one AR artwork to load reliably outdoors is manageable. Getting thirty-five of them to load reliably, on mid-tier Android phones, in direct tropical sun, over patchy 4G, at the same time across a city centre, is a different problem entirely. That was the real brief hiding underneath the creative one.

↻
Bukit Bintang touchpoint
On location

Each touchpoint was tested against direct sun glare and mid-tier Android hardware before going live.

↻
QR activation, Pasar Seni
No app required

Any iOS or Android browser could load an artwork straight from the QR code, in under three seconds.

Built to need nothing

EDT built all 35 experiences as WebAR on 8th Wall specifically to remove the app-store step entirely. A visitor's own phone browser was the only requirement. That decision drove almost everything else — asset sizes, load sequencing, how much geometry an artwork could carry before it stopped feeling instant.

Every artwork, on its own record

Because artists were being judged individually as well as collectively, each of the 35 pieces needed its own analytics, not just a festival-wide total. EDT instrumented every touchpoint separately, so artists could see their own impressions and scans in real time instead of waiting for a post-event report.

↻
Artist installation, Dataran Merdeka
Per-artwork analytics

Real-time impression and scan data, tracked independently for each of the 35 artworks.

↻
Weekend foot traffic, Downtown KL
The weekend it ran

Dense foot traffic across three precincts, all hitting the same WebAR infrastructure at once.

What held up

By the end of the weekend, the infrastructure had done what it needed to: no artwork went down under load, and the numbers were real enough to matter — not vanity metrics, but the kind of data an artist could put in their own portfolio afterward.

ARFestKL didn't need an app, an account, or a queue — just a city centre and a reason to look up. That's the version of "immersive" we'd rather build: the one that disappears into infrastructure and leaves the art doing the talking.
